headline: Request for determination for driveway work at 590 Lincoln Street, and informal discussion on 96 Tower Road project changes.
summary: The meeting covers a request for determination for removing a trench drain and restoring driveway pavement at 590 Lincoln Street. It also includes an informal discussion of reduced planned work at 96 Tower Road.
items: Request for Determination of Applicability for 590 Lincoln Street: remove a trench drain and restore driveway pavement; straw wattles and silt fence proposed. Applicant: Hobbs Brook Real Estate LLC / Peter Marino

Informal discussion for 96 Tower Road (DEP 316-0847): applicant proposed several changes, with an overall reduction of planned work. Applicant: Brad Wynnemer / Algonquin Gas. Discussion and recommendation
Correspondence: DCR did unscheduled extra invasive management work in Beaver Brook Reservation the week of 10/5 and expects to submit an annual summary report (316-0777)
Correspondence: DEP moved regional drought status back to Level 2 – Significant Drought as of October 9
Correspondence: commission office received a press inquiry about city government responsibility for drought information, water use recommendations, and water restrictions in Waltham
Councillor Logan reported possible soap or wax residue reaching the Charles River from vehicles leaving the Elm Street car wash and suggested an investigation
Site visit report: 44 Shore Road, resident report of potential dumping
Committee report: CPC next meeting scheduled for November 17
New Business: noting the passing of Louis Andrews, former commission member
New Business: possible scheduling of Paine/Storer boundary walk (November or December)

Waltham Conservation Commission 
October 22, 2026 
7:00 p.m. 
Meeting Agenda 
 
Pursuant to the relevant legislation, including Mass. Acts 2025 c.2, this meeting will take place 
remotely. All Open Meeting Law requirements will be met and public access will be available by Zoom 
call. Residents who need a device to connect are invited to use a public desktop or borrow a 
laptop at the Waltham public library (valid library card required). 
For this meeting, members of the public may participate by joining at: 
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84352947842?pwd=X313x98XbHS3kXNxGaf94D4Ri1r5vg.1  
Passcode: Waltham 
We will post a link to the video recording at http://www.wcac.org/government/meetings/conservation-
commission as soon as possible after the meeting. 
 
 
Public Meeting 
Request for Determination of Applicability 
Applicant: Hobbs Brook Real Estate LLC / Peter Marino 
Property Location: 590 Lincoln Street 
Project Description: Removal of a trench drain and restoration of driveway pavement. Straw wattles 
and silt fence are proposed to minimize disturbance to adjacent areas. 
 
 
 
Public Meeting 
Informal Discussion (Relating to DEP 316-0847) 
Applicant: Brad Wynnemer / Algonquin Gas 
Property Location: 96 Tower Road 
Description: Applicant has proposed several changes. Overall reduction of planned work. Discussion 
and recommendation. 
 
 
 
Commission Business 
• Approval of meeting minutes from 10-8-2026. 
 
Correspondence 
• INFORMATIONAL: DCR notified that they were able to perform unscheduled additional invasive 
management work in the Beaver Brook Reservation the week of 10/5. They expect to submit the 
annual summary report in the near future. [316-0777] 
• INFORMATIONAL: DEP has moved regional drought status back to “Level 2 – Significant Drought” 
as of October 9. The commission office received a local press inquiry regarding city government
responsibility for disseminating drought status information, wa ter use recommendations, and 
water restrictions in Waltham. 
• Councillor Logan has reported possible soap or wax resid ue reaching the Charles River from 
vehicles exiting the car wash on Elm Street and suggested the commission investigate. 
 
Old Business 
• Conservation Restrictions. Update. 
 
Site Visit Reports 
• 44 Shore Road. Resident report of potential dumping. 
 
Committee Reports 
• CPC: Next meeting scheduled for November 17. 
 
New Business 
• Noting the passing of Louis Andrews, former commission member. 
• Possible scheduling of Paine/Storer boundary walk (Nov./Dec.)
